To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the IP-based Internet-of-Things is a heterogeneous, distributed and dynamic environment, where the use of IP security protocols is limited due to the resource-constrained devices, and where the security solutions need to be scalable and flexible to meet the needs of different applications.

(i) the Internet of Things is an emerging paradigm for embedded systems that will be deployed in a wide variety of application domains, (ii) the security requirements for this paradigm are very similar to those in the Internet, but there are also significant differences, (iii) the current IP security protocols and mechanisms are not sufficient to provide the required level of security, and (iv) new mechanisms and solutions are required to address these limitations.
the IP security architecture is not suitable for the Internet of Things, but that the IP security protocols can be used in some cases.

the security challenges and requirements for the Internet of Things and the applicability of IP-based security mechanisms in this domain.
